facts.raw_span: A 66-year-old woman
a history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma
abdominal and pelvic pain
Physical examination was unremarkable
a creatinine level of 0.81 mg dl–1
laboratory studies, including a creatinine level, were within normal limits
a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation located in the upper pole
creating a defect in the renal parenchyma
visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, a finding known as a “renal parenchymal vascular pedicle”
a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava
No other masses or enlarged lymph nodes were identified

concepts.why: The presence of a renal mass with fat attenuation, visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, and a fatty tumor thrombus in the renal vein are characteristic findings of renal cell carcinoma.

support_spans: a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation located in the upper pole
visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, a finding known as a “renal parenchymal vascular pedicle”
contradict_spans: a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava
concepts.why: The presence of a renal mass with fat attenuation and visible vessels extending into the renal cortex are characteristic findings of angiomyolipoma, but the presence of a fatty tumor thrombus in the renal vein is more suggestive of renal cell carcinoma.
It explains the history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma in the patient.

rationales.F07: The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation is highly suggestive of a renal tumor, which could be either renal cell carcinoma or angiomyolipoma.
rationales.F09: The presence of visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, known as a renal parenchymal vascular pedicle, is more characteristic of renal cell carcinoma than angiomyolipoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava is highly suggestive of a malignant renal tumor, which could be either renal cell carcinoma or a metastasis from another primary site, such as endometrioid endometrial carcinoma.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava, which is not typical for Angiomyolipoma and lacks evidence for Endometrioid endometrial carcinoma metastasis.
